producer_report.summary: Added a code-health check. It measures each Rust file under crates/ for production lines (blank lines, whole-line comments and #[cfg(test)] items excluded), longest function (parsed with syn), landings in the last 7 days, and failure citations. A breach queues one "Structural pass: <path>" request that cites the measured numbers. Every 10th landing since the last design review queues a self-contained high-priority design-review request. The check runs after each finished job (note_finished) and after each landed pull request (land_pr, after resync_onto_merge). Cadence and dedup come from records and open requests; the only stored value is a first-review baseline file in the state directory. `athena status` now shows the table with the limits and the test suite's run time. A check that measures no file says "no files measured" and is not shown as healthy. Added D131 to docs/decisions.md and a CHANGELOG entry. Full `cargo test --locked` passed, and fmt and clippy -D warnings were clean. Departure from the plan: the two hook tests are in a new athena-cli integration test file, not in a core `code_health::hooks` module (see open_issues).

checks_run.note: 10 tests pass: measures, thresholds, structural pass dedup, cadence, review text, first review, status field, unparsable file, check that cannot run.
2 passed; with each hook call commented out, both failed with no 'code health:' line; calls restored afterwards.
The matching test ran and passed.
Full workspace suite, run once; no failures.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a code_health test with fixture source files and landing records asserts per-file production line count (excluding #[cfg(test)] modules), longest function length, landings in the last 7 days, and failure/rejection citations.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test --offline -p athena-core --lib code_health`. code_health::tests::measures_lines_longest_function_weekly_landings_and_citations_from_files_and_records writes a fixture file to a tempdir and checks 15 production lines (the cfg(test) module, blanks and comments excluded), longest function 6 (long_one, with a brace inside a string), 1 weekly landing (a landing 10 days old is excluded), and 2 citations (one finding, one outcome reason).

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: tests show a breach of each threshold (file over 2000 lines, function over 200 lines, over 1500 lines with 5 or more landings in a week) is reported, and a file under the thresholds is not flagged.
criteria_check.evidence: code_health::tests::thresholds_flag_each_breach_and_leave_a_file_under_them_alone. It flags 2001 lines, a 201-line function, and 1501 lines with 5 landings. It does not flag 2000 lines, a 200-line function, 1501 lines with 4 landings, 1500 lines with 5 landings, or a small file with 9 landings.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: on a breach exactly one structural-pass request is queued for that file, citing the measured numbers; running again, or with an open structural-pass request for that file, queues none.
criteria_check.evidence: code_health::tests::running_the_check_queues_exactly_one_structural_pass_and_a_second_run_queues_none uses a real scratch repository: one Queued request containing '2001 production lines', and the second run queues none. code_health::tests::a_breach_plans_one_structural_pass_naming_the_numbers_unless_one_is_open checks that an open request blocks a new one, another file's request does not, and a closed one does not.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: the design-review request is queued at high priority at the 10th landed job since the last review and not at the 9th.
criteria_check.evidence: code_health::tests::design_review_cadence_queues_at_high_priority_on_the_tenth_landing_not_the_ninth: with 9 landings after the last review the plan has no review; with 10 it has one and Priority::from_text(text) == Priority::High. An open review blocks the next, and the landed review job itself is not counted.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: the queued design-review text names what to review (the code-health table, files most changed and most broken since the last review, open structural-pass requests, recent rejections and planning stops) and what to produce (a short design note with proposed changes, as a design-only job).
criteria_check.evidence: code_health::tests::design_review_text_names_what_to_review_and_what_to_produce asserts the text contains 'design-only job', the table, the changed-most and broken-most files with counts, the open structural-pass request with its job id, the recent rejection with its reason, the 'Recent rejections and planning stops' heading, 'A short design note', 'proposed changes' and acceptance bullets. The test builds no planning-stop record, so only that heading is asserted.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: with no earlier review request, the first design review does not fire at once on existing history.
criteria_check.evidence: code_health::tests::the_first_review_does_not_fire_on_existing_history: 25 landings and no review give no review and baseline 25. With baseline 25, 34 landings give none and 35 give one. End to end, the first run writes code-health-baseline.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a test of the Athena::land_pr path shows the code-health check is invoked and would fail without the hook; the finished-job hook is likewise shown.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test --offline -p athena-cli --test code_health_hooks`: 2 passed. One test calls the real Athena::land_pr on the cutover fixture, with a github.com-shaped remote copy and a fake gh runner. The other runs the real Athena::go. Each asserts a 'code health:' line and exactly one queued structural-pass request. With the call commented out in gh.rs and in steward.rs, both tests failed with 'no code health line'; the calls were then restored.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: the rendered athena status output contains the code-health table with each file's lines, longest function, weekly landings, citations, thresholds, whether over, and test suite run time.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test --offline -p athena-cli status_renders_the_code_health_table` builds a full StatusView and renders display::status. It asserts the three limits, each file's lines, longest function, weekly landings, citations, the OVER marker, the breach text and 'test suite run time: 542 s'. With no files it asserts 'no files measured' and 'test suite run time: unknown'. Core test status_carries_the_code_health_table shows Athena::status fills the field.

criteria_check.criterion: cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are clean and cargo test passes.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I also ran `cargo fmt --all --check` (clean), `cargo clippy --all-targets --offline -q -- -D warnings` (clean) and `cargo test --locked -q` (all passed).

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and docs/decisions.md records the thresholds, the buy-versus-build call on measuring function length, and the 10-landing cadence.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md has a new Unreleased 'Added' entry. docs/decisions.md has D131, which records the three thresholds, the syn versus line-scan call (tree-sitter rejected), the 10-landing cadence, the baseline rule and the resync-skip note.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: the two hook tests are not a code_health::hooks module in athena-core. They are in a new file, crates/athena-cli/tests/code_health_hooks.rs, because driving the real Athena::go and Athena::land_pr needs the cutover fixture and athena-cli's capabilities, which core cannot depend on. The verifier should run `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test code_health_hooks` (expect 2 passed). That file is not in the brief's deliverable list.
crates/athena-core/src/run.rs is unchanged: no hook was needed there, because go already reaches note_finished.
If resync_onto_merge fails in land_pr, its error is propagated and the check is skipped for that landing; this is recorded in D131.
The 'planning stops' part of the design-review text is only a heading plus whatever stopped jobs exist; no test builds a stopped-planning record.

Weekly landings are attributed per file from candidate.changes of landed request jobs; citations use findings, reasons and outcome text naming the path. A rejected job that only changed the file, without naming it, is not a citation.
Existing tests print an extra 'code health:' line when a job finishes; none failed in the full run.
mistakes: The first test draft used day numbers above 30 in a date; fixed.
The first run of the structural-pass test failed because the state directory did not exist when the baseline file was written. That was a real gap in the code, so check_code_health now creates it.
I first drafted a stray hooks module with undefined helpers and removed it before compiling.
learnings: Athena::queue (athena ask --later) is reusable for queueing requests: it redacts, commits and uses the cli channel, which athena drain works.
commit_records takes the repository lock itself, so a caller must not hold lock_repository around it.
gh::parse_remote only searches the URL for 'github.com', so a local bare copy at a path like <tmp>/github.com/example/project.git passes as a GitHub remote.
With a stored Landed link, Athena::land_pr over the cutover fixture reaches its Landed branch using a fake Runner that answers only GET .../pulls/N.
Cargo.lock already held syn 2 and proc-macro2; adding span-locations only changed the lock edges, and offline resolution worked.
Both syn 2.0.119 and syn 3.0.7 are in the workspace lock; the core crate uses syn 2.
cargo fmt expands long lines, so code_health.rs came out much longer than I wrote it.
desires: A helper in test_support that builds an Athena over a scratch repository without the cutover fixture.
A way to run a core test that drives Athena::land_pr without needing athena-cli's capabilities.
